title: Control Dependency Misconception
pattern: Assuming that a compiler `barrier()` or a control flow branch (`if (r1 == 1)`) prevents a weakly ordered CPU from reordering a subsequent store before the conditional load.
why_bad: A CPU can speculative-execute branches, calculating and queuing the store in its store buffer before the load from `x` is finalized. Without an explicit memory barrier (like `smp_mb()`), the store can become globally visible before the load completes.
detection: A conditional block containing a compiler barrier (`barrier()`) but lacking a hardware memory barrier or acquire/release instructions.
counterexample: Using proper release-acquire primitives or an explicit hardware memory barrier (`smp_mb()`).
